papers.title: Sorcin phase separation restrains p53 translation via stress granules to prevent hepatic stellate cell senescence in liver fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Liver fibrosis (LF) is a dynamic process characterized by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition driven by hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation. Inducing senescence in activated HSCs can limit fibrosis. The p53-p21 signaling axis is a key regulator of cellular senescence, however, how p53 activity is precisely controlled remains undefined. Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) has emerged as an important stress-adaptive regulatory mechanism, driving the formation of stress granules (SGs) that regulate mRNA fate. Here, integrative analyses of human and murine datasets revealed that Sorcin expression is upregulated during fibrosis progression. Functional studies showed that Sorcin suppresses HSC senescence, as evidenced by reduced senescence markers, decreased SA-β-Gal positivity, and enhanced proliferative capacity. Mechanistically, elevated intracellular calcium drives Sorcin-mediated LLPS, enabling cooperation with the RNA-binding protein TIAR to nucleate SGs-like condensates. RNA immunoprecipitation, polysome profiling, dual-luciferase assays and EMSA demonstrated that TIAR directly binds TP53 mRNA and represses its translation. Consequently, TP53 mRNA is sequestered within SG-like condensates, attenuating p53 signaling and delaying HSC senescence. In vivo, AAV-mediated Sorcin knockdown enhances HSC senescence and alleviates LF in a CCl-induced mouse model. This study reveals a phase separation-mediated translational control mechanism governing HSC senescence. By restraining senescence, Sorcin sustains fibrotic persistence, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for LF.

papers.title: Trajectories of self-regulated learning patterns across medical students' transition to clerkships: A longitudinal Q-method study.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Medical education transitions are dynamic developmental processes in which learners shift between different roles and environments. The transition to clinical clerkship is a period of heightened vulnerability. While self-regulated learning (SRL) supports learning in such complex contexts, it remains unclear how students mobilise its different processes during this transition and how individual patterns emerge and change in its early phase. This study aims to capture the heterogeneity and temporal dynamics of SRL patterns by exploring how individual agency interacts with the clinical environment. METHODS: This study employed a longitudinal Q-methodology approach. The Q-set was developed based on interviews with senior medical students and expert consensus. Then, Q-sorting was conducted with 23 medical students at two time points: 1 week (T1) and 1 month (T2) after starting their clerkships. The Q-sorting data were analysed separately at each time point using factor analysis. Factor arrays and post-sorting interviews at both time points were integrated to identify SRL patterns. Participants' transitions between patterns across the two time points were tracked to map SRL trajectories. RESULTS: The Q-set comprised 44 statements. A total of 45 Q-sortings were collected (23 at T1 and 22 at T2), leading to the identification of four SRL patterns at T1 (Goal Orientation, Environmental Sensitivity, Feedback Dependence, Structural Misalignment) and four at T2 (Role-model Orientation, Structural Conflict, Proactive Challenge-Seeking, Relational Sensitivity), respectively. By tracking participants' longitudinal transitions between patterns, a Sankey diagram was used to visualise the cohort-level flows, revealing six distinct trajectories of SRL development during the clerkship transition. papers.title: More than the right ingredients: perfecting the recipe for human hematopoietic stem cell expansion.
papers.abstract: Ex vivo expansion of human hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) has long been a major objective in regenerative medicine, with the potential to improve hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, enable more effective gene therapies, and broaden patient access to curative treatments. Despite decades of investigation, preserving long-term HSC self-renewal while achieving clinically meaningful expansion has proven challenging because HSC fate is tightly regulated by intrinsic molecular programs and the specialized bone marrow microenvironment. Over the past decade, however, substantial progress has transformed the field. The discovery of small molecules that modulate key regulatory pathways, advances in chemically defined culture systems, and a growing understanding of the cellular, biochemical, and biophysical cues provided by the bone marrow niche have led to significant improvements in ex vivo HSC maintenance and expansion. In parallel, the clinical translation of several expansion platforms has demonstrated the therapeutic potential of these approaches, particularly for umbilical cord blood transplantation and genome-edited HSC therapies. This Review discusses the biological principles underlying HSC expansion, summarizes current culture strategies, and highlights recent clinical advances. We also examine the remaining challenges associated with genomic stability, manufacturing scalability, and quality control, as well as emerging in vivo gene therapy approaches. Altogether, these advances are redefining HSC engineering and provide a foundation for the next generation of regenerative and gene-based therapies.

papers.title: Serum Peptides Penetrate Dense poly(ethylene glycol) Coatings on Nanoparticles and Modulate Serum Protein Adsorption.
papers.abstract: PEGylation is a commonly used strategy to extend the systemic circulation of nanomedicines and nanocarriers by reducing serum protein adsorption and thereby limiting rapid elimination. However, even densely PEGylated nanoparticles (NPs) can undergo substantial interactions with serum components, which may compromise their circulation and therapeutic performance. This study investigates the role of circulating human serum peptides (HSPs) in modulating protein association on densely PEGylated NPs. In vitro experiments with PEGylated gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) demonstrated that pre-association of HSPs can alter subsequent serum protein association, with the magnitude and direction of the effect depending on the PEG architecture. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that, while the "brush" PEG chain obstructs direct association of human serum albumin with the AuNP surface, HSPs can access the dense PEG layers and interact directly with the AuNP surface. Under the simulated conditions, HSPs further accumulated and formed peptide clusters within the PEG layer, which provided a potential molecular basis for subsequent albumin association. Experimental studies with different PEG chain lengths and grafting densities further demonstrated that peptide-mediated modulation of protein association is dependent on the nanoparticle interfacial configuration. Moreover, peptide pre-association produced a time-dependent alteration in the circulating abundance of PEGylated AuNPs in vivo. Together, these findings suggest that serum peptides represent an underappreciated component of the nanoparticle interface that can remodel the local PEG-protein interaction environment and modulate protein association and nanoparticle fate in a context-dependent manner. papers.title: Secondary bile acids disrupt hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis caused by a high-fat diet disrupts hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) homeostasis; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we identify gut microbial secondary bile acid deoxycholic acid (DCA) as a key mediator of HSC dysfunction in mice. Plasma DCA levels were elevated during aging, consistent with previously reported increases in high-fat diet-fed mice. Chronic DCA administration upregulated Spred1 in mouse HSCs, as also observed during aging, contributing to HSC loss. DCA treatment in Spred1-deficient mice triggered myeloproliferative neoplasm-like disease, highlighting Spred1's role in mediating a trade-off between HSC aging and tumor suppression. Unexpectedly, DCA-counteracting ursodeoxycholic acid also promoted age-associated expansion of myeloid-biased mouse HSCs. In contrast, a high-fiber diet lowered plasma DCA levels and mitigated aging-associated HSC decline. Our findings reveal that systemic gut microbial metabolites, particularly secondary bile acids, critically affect HSC fate, and suggest that dietary interventions targeting the gut microbiota can regulate hematopoietic homeostasis.

papers.title: Durable and reversible epigenetic programming of human hematopoietic stem cells as a platform for modulation of platelet function.
papers.abstract: Programmable epigenome editing offers control of gene expression without altering DNA sequence, but its capacity to program human hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and their differentiated progeny remains incompletely characterized. Here, we establish that DNA methylation-based epigenome editors delivered transiently as RNA induce heritable gene silencing in primary human HSCs. Targeting the platelet integrin β3 (ITGB3) produced silencing that persisted through long-term HSC self-renewal and megakaryocytic differentiation, impaired aggregation of in vitro-derived platelets, and was partially reversed through targeted demethylation at this locus. Silencing remained stable in human HSCs 4 months after transplantation into mice. Targeting additional platelet-associated genes demonstrated broad applicability with this approach. Together, these findings establish DNA methylation-based epigenome editing as a platform for durable and reversible programming of human HSCs and demonstrate its application to modulating platelet function.

papers.title: Tumor metastasis co-opts liver hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated hematopoietic abnormalities contribute to systemic immunosuppression. However, whether tumors can initiate localized extramedullary hematopoiesis to suppress antitumor immunity remains unclear. In this study, we identify a distinct form of hepatic hematopoiesis driven by liver metastasis-associated hematopoietic stem cells (LM-HSCs). Liver metastases establish ectopic periportal hematopoietic niches that recruit bone marrow HSCs through Kupffer cell-dependent C-C motif chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1) signaling. Although LM-HSCs retain self-renewal and multipotency, cAMP response element-binding protein (CREB) activation skews their differentiation toward the myeloid lineage, particularly annexin A1-positive (ANXA1) immature neutrophils. These neutrophils produce glucocorticoids, which activate glucocorticoid receptor signaling in a paracrine manner and induce immune checkpoint receptor expression and functional anergy in CD8T and natural killer cells. Collectively, these findings suggest that liver metastases reprograms hepatic hematopoiesis to promote immunosuppression.

papers.title: Multimodal omics identifies a lymphoid-biased multipotent progenitor population with limited age-associated remodeling.
papers.abstract: Hematopoietic aging is marked by declining regenerative capacity and a shift from lymphoid to myeloid output. Previous studies have focused primarily on hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), yet whether aging uniformly remodels the hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) compartment, or selectively affects distinct populations, remains largely unknown. To address this, we profile HSCs and multipotent progenitors MPP1-6 from young and aged mice across transcriptomic, epigenomic, metabolomic and lipidomic layers, together with single-cell division and in vivo serial transplantation assays. We identify young MPP6 (negative for CD150, CD34, CD48 and CD135) as an HSC-like, lymphoid-biased population with long-term reconstitution capacity, positioned within the top-tier of the differentiation hierarchy and marked by low global chromatin accessibility and metabolic activity. Upon aging, MPP6 preserved long-term lymphoid reconstitution, underwent limited transcriptional and regulatory remodeling, and did not accumulate polyunsaturated phospholipids or show mitochondrial oxidation. By contrast, most HSPCs, and particularly HSCs, underwent pronounced age-associated changes, including myeloid-biased expansion, metabolic rewiring, extensive distal regulatory alteration and accumulation of long-chain polyunsaturated phospholipids linked to increased oxidative stress. Pseudotime analysis further resolved the aged MPP6 compartment into two subsets, including a dormant, lymphoid-biased Dlk1-expressing population characterized by reduced mitochondrial activity, which was distinctly affected by inflammatory challenge in vivo. Together, these findings establish MPP6 as a comparatively resilient population within the aged HSPC compartment and suggest that it may represent a potential target for restoring hematopoietic balance.

papers.title: Less is more: expanding human HSCs via a novel mimetic niche.
Impact of environmental factors on cardiovascular health in Castilla-La Mancha: the CarVasCLiMa cohort study protocol.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The CarVasCLiMa project aims to investigate the associations between environmental factors and cardiovascular health outcomes in the population of Castilla-La Mancha. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The study will include a representative cohort of residents from urban, semiurban and rural areas, followed over a 2-year period. Environmental exposure variables, including air pollution and climate conditions, will be assessed using high-resolution satellite data complemented by data from local monitoring stations. Proximity to green spaces will be estimated using the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index and geospatial data. Cardiovascular outcomes will include measurements of blood pressure, arterial stiffness and circulating biomarkers such as C-reactive protein. In addition, validated questionnaires will be administered to assess quality of life, emotional well-being and lifestyle factors. Data analysis will involve advanced statistical modelling to examine longitudinal associations between environmental and lifestyle factors and cardiovascular outcomes, including sex-stratified analyses and specific evaluations of vulnerable population subgroups. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This protocol was previously approved by the Clinical Research Ethics Committee of the Health Area in the city of Cuenca (REG: 2025/PI1625). This approach will enable the identification of differential susceptibility to environmental and lifestyle factors and support the development of targeted prevention strategies. Finally, the findings of this study are expected to inform the development of public health policies tailored to the regional context, contributing to the mitigation of environmental risks and the improvement of cardiovascular health and overall quality of life in Castilla-La Mancha.

papers.title: A Carrier-Free, Co-assembled Nanoplatform for Synergistic Photothermal Therapy: Integrating High-Efficiency BODIPY with Heat Shock Protein Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: The simultaneous delivery of boron-dipyrromethene (BODIPY) photosensitizers and heat shock proteins (HSPs) inhibitors to tumor sites can enhance the therapeutic efficacy of photothermal therapy (PTT). Current strategies mainly rely on physical encapsulation into nanocarriers or chemical conjugation onto polymer backbones for the co-delivery of BODIPY and HSP inhibitors. However, these approaches are hampered by drug leakage, reproducibility, or synthetic polydispersity. Herein, we report a carrier-free, co-assembled, and self-delivery nanoplatform to overcome these limitations. An amphiphilic BODIPY derivative (BODIPY-OEG) was synthesized and co-assembled with HSP inhibitors quercetin (Q), yielding nanoparticles (B@Q) with high photothermal conversion efficiency. The resulting B@Q nanoparticles not only possessed favorable photothermal performance in vitro but also had been demonstrated to possess potent antitumor capabilities by inhibiting the expression of HSPs in tumor cells. In vivo, B@Q demonstrated potent antitumor activity by suppressing subcutaneous tumor growth and lung metastasis, while also eliciting a potent systemic immune response, demonstrating its excellent antitumor efficacy. This work proposes a simple and precise co-assembly strategy to construct carrier-free, multifunctional nanotherapeutics, which opens avenues for the concept of self-delivered synergistic PTT agents.

papers.title: Phenological divergence between flowering plants and flower-visiting Lepidoptera under climate change across Europe.
papers.abstract: Climate change is altering life-cycle timing and may disrupt coordinated interactions between flowering plants and flower-visiting insects. Using Global Biodiversity Information Facility observation records from Europe between 2000 and 2024, we compiled a continental-scale phenological dataset covering flowering periods of 707 angiosperm species and adult activity periods of 620 Lepidoptera species. We extracted the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles and activity-window width and used linear mixed-effects models to analyse spatio-temporal trends. The results showed that plant phenology advanced significantly, with the 10th and 50th percentiles shifting earlier by -0.597 and -0.507 d yr⁻¹, respectively, whereas the 90th percentile showed no significant change; flowering-window width increased by 0.361 d yr⁻¹. By contrast, Lepidoptera phenology advanced evenly across the season, with the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles shifting by -0.137, -0.153 and -0.155 d yr⁻¹, respectively, while activity-window width showed no significant change. Because flowering plants advanced faster than Lepidoptera in the early and middle season, plant-insect phenological overlap declined at 0.340 d yr⁻¹, indicating increasing mismatch across Europe. Further analyses identified temperature as the dominant driver of phenological advance in both groups, but flowering plants and Lepidoptera differed in their responses to other climatic factors. These results suggest that climate change is weakening phenological synchrony between flowering plants and flower-visiting Lepidoptera, with potential consequences for pollination and ecosystem functioning.

papers.title: Regulation of hepatic stellates cell activation by biomimetic fibrotic hydrogels with uniform and heterogeneous matrix stiffness.
papers.abstract: Current research on liver fibrosis predominantly relies on culture matrices with uniform stiffness, largely overlooking the pathophysiological relevance of stiffness heterogeneity-the spatially uneven stiffness distribution characteristic of fibrotic liver tissue. To address this, we engineered biomimetic fibrotic hydrogels using decellularized liver matrix (DLM) from fibrotic tissues and methacrylated hyaluronic acid (MeHA). These hydrogels replicated the distinct stiffness profiles of normal, earlystage fibrotic, and late-stage fibrotic liver. Using a custom honeycomb-shaped mold, we integrated them into a unified platform featuring both uniform and heterogeneous mechanical regions. By co-culturing hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) on this platform, we investigated how matrix stiffness regulates HSCs proliferation, migration, and activation. Results demonstrated that on uniformly stiff substrates, particularly those mimicking late-stage fibrosis, ECM components and high stiffness promoted HSCs activation, upregulated the Piezo1-YAP signaling axis. In contrast, although the lowstiffness region of the mechanically heterogeneous platform exhibited increased HSC proliferation and activation, the proliferation and activation levels in the medium-and high-stiffness regions were significantly reduced. The expression patterns of the Piezo1-YAP signaling pathway further corroborated this phenomenon. These findings suggest that mechanical heterogeneity may exert a negative regulatory effect on HSC activation. This study provides new insights into the mechanobiological mechanisms underlying hepatic fibrosis and reveals potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: HSPiP, computational, and thermodynamic models-based solubility validation of tofacitinib in PEG400 - water system, shelf-life estimation, and GastroPlus-enabled predictive in vivo performance.
papers.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The subcutaneous (sub-Q) delivery of tofacitinib citrate (TOFA) can be a promising alternative to overcome oral associated side effects and complications . OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to address HSPiP based predicted solubility and solubility behaviour of TOFA in various mass ratios (m = 0.0-1.0) of PEG400 in PEG400-water system T = 298.15-318.15 K. METHODS: Hansen solubility parameters were estimated and the experimental solubility data were validated using various models (Van't Hoff, Apelblat, Roseman-Yalkowsky, and thermodynamic models). Finally, the stability study was conducted to estimate TOFA shelf-life, followed by GastroPlus-based predictive in vivo performance in humans. RESULTS: PEG400 addition resulted in reduced δand δvalues up to m = 0.5, which may be correlated to the effective disruption of extensive H-bond network strength and decreased overall polarity of water by PEG400, as predicted in HSPiP. The temperature-dependent solubility was validated with the models. The binary system (m = 0.5) exhibited stable solubility, suitable for sub-Q delivery. The enthalpy-entropy compensation temperature (T) was 59.5 °C, suggesting constant ΔG° over m = 0.1-0.9 of PEG400. Thus, TOFA solubility and stability were temperature, mass, and pH dependent. GastroPlus software predicted improved pharmacokinetic parameters and extended in vivo absorption following sub-Q delivery at m = 0.5 in humans. CONCLUSION: Thus, a stable sub-Q product can be a promising alternative to the conventional tablet of TOFA.

papers.title: Sensory processing sensitivity profiles and self-reported mental effort and concentration across pedagogical contexts among social services and healthcare students: a cross-sectional study.
papers.journal: Advances in health sciences education : theory and practice
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Changes in higher education and evolving pedagogical practices have increased the diversity of cognitive, emotional, and social demands experienced by students, highlighting the need to understand individual differences, including sensory processing sensitivity (SPS). AIM: To identify SPS profiles among social services and healthcare students and examine whether self-reported mental effort and concentration across selected pedagogical contexts differed between the profiles. DESIGN: A cross-sectional study. PARTICIPANTS: 1185 social and healthcare higher education students across Finland. METHODS: The data were collected with the SPS Questionnaire (43 items) during 2024-2025. K-means clustering and One-way ANOVA were employed to analyse the profiles of SPS. The associated pedagogical factors were analysed using Chi-square tests. The STROBE guidelines were followed. RESULTS: Five distinct SPS profiles emerged, differing significantly in sensitivity, emotional reactivity, and pedagogical responses. Profiles characterised by higher emotional and physiological reactivity (Profiles 2, 4, and 5) generally reported greater mental effort and more concentration difficulties, particularly in socially demanding and performance-based situations such as group work, oral presentations, and simulations. In contrast, low-reactive profiles (Profiles 1 and 3) demonstrated stable concentration and lower cognitive load across learning contexts. CONCLUSIONS: Pedagogical methods do not influence all students equally. Instructional approaches that involve intense social interaction, performance exposure, or high cognitive demands may disproportionately increase stress and cognitive load for highly reactive learners. Designing inclusive, psychologically safe, and adaptive learning environments that consider SPS-related differences can support student well-being, learning effectiveness, and sustainable professional development in social and healthcare education.

papers.title: Bcl11a preserves hematopoietic stem cell function in culture by restraining Ncf1-dependent ROS.
papers.abstract: Ex vivo expansion of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) is limited by culture-induced oxidative stress, yet the upstream transcriptional drivers remain poorly defined. Here, we show that the transcription factor Bcl11a is rapidly and persistently downregulated during HSC culture and that this decline drives functional deterioration. Bcl11a was both required and sufficient to maintain quiescence, clonogenic activity, and serially transplantable HSC function. Mechanistically, Bcl11a directly represses a Nox2 NADPH oxidase gene module, including Ncf1, encoding the p47phox organizer subunit; Ncf1 deletion reduced ROS and partially rescued the defects of Bcl11a-deficient HSCs. Rapamycin-but not the ROS scavenger N-acetylcysteine-restored Bcl11a expression, suppressed Ncf1 and ROS, and improved HSC function, identifying Bcl11a as a candidate effector linking mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 inhibition to redox control. This axis was conserved in human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, revealing a druggable transcriptional vulnerability of cultured HSCs and a framework for improving ex vivo-expanded grafts.

papers.title: Hinokitiol alleviates liver fibrosis in rats: Plausible role of hepatic stellate cell activation and TGF-β/Smad2/3 axis.
papers.abstract: Liver fibrosis represents a progressive pathological condition with excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition, primarily driven by hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) activation and sustained inflammatory and oxidative stress responses. Despite its clinical burden, effective antifibrotic therapies remain limited. Here, we investigated the therapeutic potential of hinokitiol (HKT), a natural tropolone derivative, in attenuating liver fibrosis using both in vitro and in vivo models. Human LX-2 HSCs were employed to assess the mechanistic effects of HKT under TGF-β-induced fibrogenic conditions. HKT treatment significantly suppressed myofibroblastic transdifferentiation, as evidenced by downregulation of α-SMA, N-cadherin, vimentin, and collagen I, and reduced HSC migration. Additionally, HKT attenuated reactive oxygen species generation via inhibition of NADPH oxidase 4 (NOX4) expression. In an experimental model of alcohol- and carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)-induced liver fibrosis, oral administration of HKT (2.5, 5, and 10 mg/kg) significantly ameliorated hepatic injury, as indicated by reduced serum ALT and AST levels, improved liver morphology, and restored hepatic architecture. Histopathological and biochemical analyses revealed a pronounced reduction in collagen deposition, hydroxyproline content, and fibrotic bridging. Mechanistically, HKT suppressed the TGF-β/Smad2/3 cascade, thereby inhibiting HSCs activation and ECM accumulation. Furthermore, HKT reduced the expression of lysyl oxidase-like 2 (LOXL2) protein, which further impeded the stiffening of fibrous liver. In addition, HKT mitigated hepatic oxidative stress, while concurrently attenuating pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and IL-1β. Taken together, our findings establish HKT as a potential candidate to limit fibrosis progression and hepatic tissue remodeling by impeding HSCs activation and the TGF-β/Smad2/3/LOXL2 cascade.

papers.title: TDQ-Cl ameliorates hepatic fibrosis-associated inflammation and intestinal injury through regulating RXRα-STAT3 signaling.
papers.abstract: Hepatic fibrosis is sustained by inflammation-driven hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) activation and is frequently accompanied by intestinal barrier disruption and gut microbial dysbiosis. 2,3,9,10-tetramethoxy-5,6-dihydroisoquinolino[3,2-a]isoquinolin-7-ium chloride (TDQ-Cl) is a quaternary isoquinoline alkaloid with anti-inflammatory activity and emerging hepatoprotective potential. This study investigated the hepatoprotective effects and underlying mechanisms of TDQ-Cl against hepatic fibrosis and associated intestinal injury. HSC-T6 and LX-2 were activated by transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β) and treated with TDQ-Cl, retinoic acid (RA), LG100268 or UVI 3003. RXRα-silenced LX-2 was stimulated with TGF-β and treated with TDQ-Cl. C57BL/6 J mice were intraperitoneally injected with thioacetamide (TAA), followed by TDQ-Cl, silymarin or RA administration. In activated HSCs, TDQ-Cl reduced extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation, IL-6, cleaved caspase-1, mature IL-1β, and STAT3 phosphorylation while restoring RXRα expression. Cellular thermal shift assay showed increased thermal stability of RXRα following TDQ-Cl treatment. RXRα silencing exacerbated fibrotic responses and attenuated the inhibitory effects of TDQ-Cl on p-STAT3, α-SMA, and IL-6. Co-immunoprecipitation indicated that TDQ-Cl reduced the association between RXRα and phosphorylated STAT3. In TAA-induced mice, TDQ-Cl attenuated liver injury, ECM accumulation, inflammation, and hepatic STAT3 phosphorylation while restoring hepatic RXRα expression. TDQ-Cl also improved intestinal barrier integrity, reduced macrophage infiltration and STAT3 phosphorylation, restored colonic RXRα expression, and partially normalized TAA-associated gut microbial alterations. papers.title: Aqueous Ammonium Ion Hybrid Supercapacitor: A Diffusion Dynamics Perspective.
papers.abstract: Aqueous ammonium-ion hybrid supercapacitors (A-HSCs) have emerged as a promising energy storage technology, offering intrinsic safety, low cost, environmental sustainability. However, the realization of these advantages hinges critically on the diffusion dynamics of the ammonium ion (NH), which remain incompletely understood and require systematic elucidation of the underlying mechanisms and optimization strategies. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in NHdiffusion kinetics within A-HSCs, approached from three interconnected perspectives: electrode materials, electrolyte engineering, and charge carrier structure. We systematically summarize the kinetic characteristics and structural design strategies for four representative classes of electrode materials-layered compounds, tunnel structures, Prussian blue analogs (PBAs), and organic frameworks-that govern NHtransport. In parallel, we elucidate how concentrated electrolytes, additive electrolytes, and high-entropy electrolytes (HEEs) reconfigure the hydrogen-bond network of water to modulate the solvation environment. Furthermore, we explore the unique diffusion behavior arising from the intrinsic tetrahedral geometry of NHand the influence of hydrogen isotope substitution, which provides a powerful experimental lever for disentangling the coupled contributions of mass, rotational inertia, and hydrogen-bond strength to the diffusion dynamics. Finally, we identify current limitations and challenges, and outline future directions for the development of high-performance aqueous ammonium-ion energy storage devices.

papers.title: Hepatic Stellate Cells: Fibrogenic Effectors to Central Regulators of Metabolism, Liver Disease Signaling, and Systemic Crosstalk.
papers.abstract: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) have long been regarded as the core effector cells in liver fibrosis. The advent of single-cell omics and metabolomics has led to a paradigm shift in our understanding of these cells. Notably, they are not only implicated in local fibrosis but are being increasingly recognized as a hub integrating metabolic and immune signaling. Located at the interface between hepatic vasculature and parenchyma, HSCs have the capacity to modulate intestinal barrier function, neurotransmitter circulation, myocardial energy metabolism, and bone remodeling through metabolic reprogramming (enhanced glycolysis, vitamin A consumption, glutamine metabolism remodeling) and receptor signaling (TLR4, TGF-β, CXCR4, etc.), as well as by secreting metabolites, exosomal miRNAs, and cytokines. Concurrently, HSCs perceive feedback signals from these organs, forming a dynamic cross-organ feedback network. This review systematically integrates the metabolic characteristics of HSCs in diseases such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, alcohol-related liver disease, chronic viral hepatitis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, along with their cross-organ interactive effects. We further discuss intervention strategies targeting metabolic pathways, exosomal cargo, and the microbiota-metabolism axis, and propose a three-tier translational framework stratifying HSC-targeted therapeutic approaches by developmental stage, offering novel insights for shifting liver disease treatment from single antifibrotic approaches toward systemic, multi-organ precision interventions.

papers.title: Ginsenoside Rh1 exerts hepatoprotective effects against liver fibrosis through induction of ferroptosis via SLC7A11 inhibition.
papers.journal: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology
papers.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a critical pathological stage in the progression from chronic liver disease to cirrhosis, and the exploration of preventive agents derived from traditional Chinese medicine offers considerable potential. However, the precise role and molecular mechanism of ginsenoside Rh1 (Rh1) in liver fibrosis remain largely obscure. This study investigated the anti-fibrotic mechanism of Rh1, focusing on ferroptosis. In vitro, Rh1 dose-dependently suppressed the viability of activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) and concurrently induced key ferroptosis features. In vivo, Rh1 administration markedly attenuated carbon tetrachloride-induced liver fibrosis, improved histological architecture, and restored liver function. Mechanistically, transcriptomic analysis and molecular validation identified SLC7A11, a core regulator of ferroptosis, as a binding partner of Rh1. Rescue experiments confirmed that the pro-ferroptotic and anti-fibrotic effects of Rh1 were functionally dependent on SLC7A11 inhibition. In conclusion, our findings demonstrated that ginsenoside Rh1 alleviated liver fibrosis by targeting SLC7A11 to promote the ferroptosis in cultured HSCs, unveiling a novel pharmacological mechanism. This work provided a compelling preclinical rationale for developing Rh1 as a promising preventive agent against liver fibrosis.

papers.title: Imaging and Analyzing the Macrophages that Regulate Pathological Hematopoietic Clones in the Mouse Calvarial Bone Marrow.
papers.abstract: The bone marrow microenvironment has been shown to regulate the progression of myeloid neoplasms. Given that bone remodeling is a dynamic process that releases bone particles as danger molecules into the bone marrow space, different stages of bone turnover across marrow cavities can impose spatial heterogeneity of inflammatory responses that impact both healthy and mutant hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs). Specifically, macrophages, serving as critical members in the HSC niche, can adopt either pro-inflammatory (M1) or anti-inflammatory (M2) phenotypes based on these local signals, which results in distinct surface receptor expression and cytokine secretion. Using intravital microscopy, a murine model of Tet2 deficiency (a prevalent mutation across the spectrum of myeloid disorders), and labeling strategies to track marrow macrophages, our recent work identified compartmentalized inflammatory landscapes in the bone marrow that differentially support expansion of mutant cells. In this chapter, we describe detailed protocols to track pathological clones with respect to marrow macrophage in live mouse calvaria, and protocols of image-guided bone button isolation to analyze pro-inflammatory cytokines from the marrow cavities of interest. These protocols can also be integrated with cell isolation for single-cell transcriptomic profiling or downstream functional assessments. The labeling strategies may be applied to image macrophages in other tissue types.

papers.title: The orthographic mind: Orthographic imagery propensity correlates with semantic structure and sensory sensitivity.
papers.abstract: Individuals differ in their habitual use of internal representational modes, including visual imagery, internal verbalization, and orthographic imagery (the mental simulation of written word forms). The present research examined whether such internal representational propensities relate to semantic organization and external information engagement. Across two studies (total N = 1,399), we assessed individuals' internal representational modes using the Internal Representations Questionnaire and examined their associations with semantic structure (nine-word semantic rating experiments; N = 1,109) and external information engagement (sensory-processing sensitivity and mobile app usage). Orthographic imagery showed robust associations with both semantic geometry and external information engagement patterns: Individuals with stronger orthographic imagery showed greater cross-category semantic association strength, lower semantic conformity, and lower sensory-processing sensitivity. Internal verbalization was positively associated with within-category semantic cohesion, while visual imagery showed no reliable associations with semantic geometry and limited associations with real-world media engagement. Effects were modest but consistent across experiments. These findings suggest that internal representational modes function as stable weighting biases, subtly modulating semantic geometry and sensory-processing profiles. Such propensities therefore correspond to structured variations in cognition, rather than merely phenomenological differences in inner experience.
